scope: Proposition 6.3 (Removal of a rough step) of the manuscript “Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers” (preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 164 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ab835f6a98c10d6d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 41-42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix G/Γ, a number d ≥ 1 of spatial variables, a degree bound D, and constants c, C, B > 0. Along an arbitrary sequence w → ∞, let L, S, Z satisfy W | L, L is w-smooth, S → ∞, S/L → ∞, Z/Sa → ∞ for every fixed a > 0. (6.9) Fix a residue r modulo L with gcd(r, W) = 1, and put T = [S, 2S) ∩ (r + LZ). Let Pt(x) be G-valued, with logarithmic coordinates polynomial jointly in (t, x) ∈ R × Rd of total degree at most D. These polynomials and their coefficients may change with w. 41 For every η > 0, the proportion of t ∈ T for which there exist a box Q ⊆ [−CZ, CZ]d with all sides at least cZ, a vector b ∈ Zd, and an observable F : G/Γ → C with ∥F∥Lip ≤ B, such that |Ex∈Q∩Zd F(Pt(x)Γ) − Ex∈Q∩(b+tZd)F(Pt(x)Γ)| ≥ η (6.10) tends to zero. This conclusion holds for every sequence of the allowed data. In particular the exceptional proportion is uniform over the polynomial coefficients, the residue r, and all the boxes, residue vectors and observables in (6.10). The latter three may be chosen separately for every t without any polynomial dependence. The same conclusion holds for a fixed finite list of nilmanifolds and fixed complexity bounds.
